title: Cloud Engines (e.g. Voxtral)
desc: Optional, opt-in cloud engines enabled with an API key — none are installed by default.
lede: Cloud engines are optional. You enable one with an API key; none ship or run by default. Voxtral (Mistral-hosted) is one example.
body:
At a glance
  • Optional and opt-in — off until you enable one.
  • Enabled with an API key.
  • Some data leaves your machine when used.
  • Voxtral is one example of this kind of engine.

Why cloud engines are optional

Studio is local-first. Cloud engines exist for people who want a specific hosted voice or model, but they are never required and never on by default.

Enabling a cloud engine with an API key

Add the provider's API key in Settings to enable it. Until a key is present, the engine stays hidden. Voxtral, for example, is enabled with a Mistral API key.

What data leaves your machine

Using a cloud engine sends the text to be spoken (and any required reference audio) to the provider. Studio discloses this clearly. See Local-First & Privacy.

Heads up — a cloud engine means data leaves your device. Review the provider's terms; Studio shows facts, it doesn't act as a legal gate.

When to use one

Reach for a cloud engine when you specifically want a voice or model it offers. For most local audiobook production, the default local engine is enough.
